note: ARES Phase 3 image records. Every record was checked against a NASA/JPL page on 2026-11-15. null means not verified or not available. No image has verified map coordinates.

images.title: Curiosity on the Road to Boxwork Formations
images.description: Morning-light Mastcam panorama of wind-carved valleys on Mount Sharp. The distant butte nicknamed Gould Mesa has a cliff band and dark ridges that may be the first glimpses of boxwork. This is an interpretation, not a confirmed identification.
images.fullSizeNote: Original JPEG is about 32 MB. Do not load it automatically.
images.limits: The page's search-engine description gives 18 Nov 2020 (sol 2946), which conflicts with the page text (9 March 2025, sol 4476). ARES uses the page text. Map location of the view is not published in the source.

images.title: Curiosity Surveys the Boxwork Region
images.description: Mastcam panorama of boxwork formations: low ridges with hollows between them. NASA's caption says groundwater minerals hardened the ridges and wind later removed the softer rock around them.
images.limits: Publication date is taken from the JPL image page (23 Feb 2026). Image file link is the web version used in NASA's article (1024 px wide); the original download link was not verified. Map location of the view is not published in the source.

images.title: Curiosity Studies Nodules on Boxwork Formations
images.description: Close-up mosaic of 50 MAHLI images (10 focus settings at each of 5 locations). Pea-sized nodules sit along ridge walls and in hollows, not near the central fractures. The wavy ridges between nodule groups are calcium sulfate veins, per NASA's caption.
images.limits: NASA does not state where on the map this was taken. A version with a scale bar (Figure A) exists on the source page.
